name: Cooperative Banking (Credit Unions & Mutual Societies)
region: Global (Germany, Ireland, India, Canada, Kenya, Japan)
summary: Member-owned financial institutions that pool savings and issue loans without shareholder profit extraction, formalising mutual-aid principles from ROSCAs and cowrie networks into regulated banking.

claims.statement: Raiffeisen's rural credit cooperatives (1864) and Schulze-Delitzsch's urban ones (1849) independently solved credit access for populations excluded by commercial banks
Credit unions now serve over 400 million members in 118 countries, demonstrating replication at scale without loss of cooperative structure
Cooperative banks proved more resilient than commercial banks during the 2008 financial crisis, with lower failure rates and continued lending

evidence.source: Raiffeisen (1866) Die Darlehnskassen-Vereine (The Credit Union Associations), Neuwied
Birchall (2013) Resilience in a Downturn: The Power of Financial Cooperatives, ILO
World Council of Credit Unions (2023) Statistical Report — 118 countries, 400M+ members
Groeneveld & de Vries (2009) European Co-operative Banks: First Lessons from the Subprime Crisis, International Journal of Cooperative Management 4(2)

notes: Resolves 4 inbound links (rotating_credit, microfinance, cowrie_currency, silk_road). Fails longevity threshold (176yr vs 300) but strong on replication and decentralisation. Interesting proof case: the scoring system correctly identifies this as 'not yet a keystone' despite massive global adoption.
